No Silver Dollar

Game Strategy

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)

Game: Move counters left along the row without jumping over another counter; the player with no move loses.
How to play: Select a counter, then choose an empty space to its left; you may move it any distance but cannot pass or share a space. Check Set up to move counters freely, then uncheck it to play.

Choose a counter, then one of the empty spaces to its left.

Look for the math

The spaces between counters hide heaps that behave like a familiar take-away game. A counter move can change a gap in a surprising direction, which is why this is sometimes called Bogus Nim.

Read the gaps as heaps

Start at the rightmost counter. The empty spaces before it form one heap. Skip the next gap, then count the next; continue alternating. If there is an odd number of counters, the spaces from the left edge to the leftmost counter form the last heap. Each legal move changes just one of these heaps.

Why some gaps grow

A counter can move left across a gap that belongs to the other parity, making that heap larger. The opponent can undo that increase immediately, so it gives no lasting advantage. Such a reversible move does not improve a player's position.

Use the Nim sum

For the heaps, calculate their Nim sum by XORing their sizes. A zero sum is losing with perfect play. Otherwise, reduce one heap so the new XOR is zero; the applet's computer uses this rule and makes a random legal move when its position is already losing.

Try a few starting boards with three counters. Count alternate gaps from the right, then see whether your first move can make their XOR zero.
